literal: Under the Zhou system, those enfeoffed with five grades of commandery and county nobility all added "Founder of the State";
idiomatic: Under Zhou, five-grade commandery and county enfeoffments all added Founder of the State;

literal: those granted Pillar of State, Opening Office, or Equal in Honor all also added "Commissioned with Staff" and "Great Commander";

literal: those appointed Commander-in-Chief or Inspector added "Commissioned with Staff" and "Commander of All Military Affairs."
idiomatic: commanders-in-chief and inspectors added Commissioned with Staff and Commander of All Military Affairs.

literal: This was the constant rule.
idiomatic: That was the constant rule.

literal: In the first year of the Daxiang era, an edict ordered commanders-in-chief, inspectors, and those on campaign to hold staffs of authority; all others were abolished.
idiomatic: Daxiang year 1: commanders, inspectors, and field armies kept staffs; all others lost them.

literal: After what Bian had fixed, there were further reforms.
idiomatic: After Bian's codification there were further reforms.

literal: Here they are roughly appended.
idiomatic: They are roughly appended below.

literal: Bian's younger brother Guang.
idiomatic: Bian's younger brother was Guang.

literal: Guang's son Jingren.
idiomatic: Guang's son was Jingren.

literal: Gentle and careful in nature, he read widely, was expert in the Three Rites, skilled in yin-yang lore, understood pitch-pipes and musical scales, and also loved Dark Learning.
idiomatic: Gentle and careful, widely read, expert in the Three Rites, yin-yang, pitch-pipes, and Dark Learning.

literal: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era he left the purple and was made a staff officer in the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: In Xiaochang's opening years he entered service as a Ministry of Works staff officer.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Guang raised righteous forces in Shandong and was appointed Inspector of Jin from afar.
idiomatic: When Xiaowu moved west, Guang raised forces in Shandong and was remotely made Jin inspector.

literal: In the sixth year of Datong he brought his family west, was made Recorder in the Chancellor's Office, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang.
idiomatic: In Datong 6 he went west with his family, became the chancellor's recorder, and was made Marquis of Fanyang.

literal: Soon he was made Mobile Secretariat Gentleman in charge of records and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anxi.
idiomatic: Soon he was mobile secretariat gentleman in charge of records, enfeoffed Marquis of Anxi.

literal: He served as Administrator of Jingzhao, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Equal in Honor with the Three Dukes, Master of Craftsmen in the Inner Court, was advanced to Duke of Yancheng and Inspector of Yu, and was Acting Chief Clerk of the Shaanzhou Commander's Office; he died in office.
idiomatic: He was Jingzhao administrator, attendant, equal in honor, master of craftsmen, advanced to Duke of Yancheng and Yu inspector, acting chief clerk at Shaanzhou headquarters, and died in office.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou had once studied under Guang as a youth, so funeral gifts exceeded the usual rule; he was posthumously made Junior Tutor with posthumous title Jian.
idiomatic: Zhou Emperor Wu had studied under him, so gifts exceeded custom; he was posthumously junior tutor, posthumous title Jian.

literal: Guang revered Buddhism and was utterly sincere in faith.
idiomatic: Guang revered Buddhism with utter sincerity.

literal: He once followed Zhou Emperor Wen on a hunt at Tanshan; when the beaters had closed the ring, the Emperor pointed to the mountain and asked the lords, "Do you gentlemen see anything?"
idiomatic: Once on a hunt at Tanshan with Emperor Wen, when the ring closed the emperor pointed uphill and asked, "Do you see anything?"

literal: " All said they saw nothing.
idiomatic: All said they saw nothing.

literal: " Guang alone said, "I see a monk."
idiomatic: Guang alone said, "I see a monk."

literal: The Emperor said, "That is so."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "So it is."

literal: " He at once lifted the encirclement and returned.
idiomatic: He lifted the encirclement and returned.

literal: He had Guang build a pagoda where the monk had stood.
idiomatic: He had Guang build a pagoda where the monk stood.

literal: When they dug the foundation one zhang down, they found a pottery bowl and an iron staff; the Emperor marveled and thereupon founded a monastery.
idiomatic: Digging one zhang down they found a bowl and iron staff; the emperor marveled and founded a monastery.

literal: When he became Administrator of Jingzhao, the prefectural residence had long had uncanny occurrences, and successive prefects dared not live there.
idiomatic: As Jingzhao administrator the yamen had long been haunted and no prefect dared live there.

literal: Guang said, "Fortune and misfortune depend on men; demons do not act without cause."
idiomatic: Guang said, "Fortune depends on men; demons do not act without cause."

literal: " He then moved in.
idiomatic: He moved in.

literal: Before long the horse Guang rode suddenly climbed the desk platform, mounted the bed, and stood facing south.
idiomatic: Soon his horse climbed the desk platform, mounted the bed, and stood facing south.

literal: Food vessels broke for no reason.
idiomatic: Food vessels broke without cause.

literal: Guang took none of it to heart—such was his sincere uprightness.
idiomatic: Guang took none of it to heart—such was his sincerity.

literal: His Expository Chapters on the Dao De Jing circulated in the world.
idiomatic: His Expository Chapters on the Dao De Jing circulated.

literal: Son Ben.
idiomatic: His son was Ben.

literal: Ben, styled Zizheng.
idiomatic: Ben, styled Zizheng.

literal: He had some acquaintance with writing and was fairly skilled in pitch-pipes and scales.
idiomatic: He knew writing somewhat and understood pitch-pipes.

literal: Under Zhou he inherited the dukedom of Yancheng and served as Administrator of Luyang, Junior Palace Master of the Heir Apparent, Equal in Honor with the Three Dukes, and Senior Master of Martial Display.
idiomatic: Under Zhou he inherited Yancheng, was Luyang administrator, junior palace master, equal in honor, and senior master of martial display.

literal: At that time Yang Jian was Grand Marshal; Ben knew he was no ordinary man and attached himself deeply.
idiomatic: When Yang Jian was grand marshal, Ben saw he was no ordinary man and attached himself deeply.

literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ben was given an Opening Office.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ben received an opening office.

literal: When Emperor Wen was entrusted on his deathbed and opinion was not yet united, he kept Ben at his side.
idiomatic: When Wen was entrusted on his deathbed and opinion was divided, he kept Ben close.

literal: The Emperor was about to go to the Eastern Residence; the hundred officials did not know where to go; the Emperor secretly ordered Ben to array guards and weapons, then summoned the lords and said, "Whoever wants wealth and honor should follow me!
idiomatic: About to go to the Eastern Residence while officials wavered, the emperor secretly had Ben array guards, then told the lords, "Who wants wealth and honor should follow me!

literal: " People whispered among themselves, wanting to stay or go.
idiomatic: Men whispered, unsure whether to stay or go.

literal: Ben came with stern troops and none dared move.
idiomatic: Ben came with stern troops and none dared move.

literal: They went out Chongyang Gate to the Eastern Palace; the gatekeepers refused entry; Ben urged them in vain, then glared and shouted, and the gatekeepers fell back.
idiomatic: At Chongyang Gate the Eastern Palace gatekeepers refused entry; Ben urged, then shouted, and they fell back.

literal: The Emperor then entered; Ben constantly directed the night guard and seized chances to urge responding to Heaven and following the people; the Emperor followed him.
idiomatic: Once inside, Ben ran the night guard and urged responding to Heaven and the people; the emperor followed.

literal: When he received the abdication, he ordered Ben to clear the palace and again put him in charge of the night guard.
idiomatic: On receiving the throne he had Ben clear the palace and again run the night guard.

literal: Ben memorialized to change Zhou banners and give them auspicious names; the Azure Dragon, Zouyu, Vermilion Bird, Black Tortoise, Thousand Autumns, and Ten Thousand Years banners were all his creations.
idiomatic: Ben memorialized to change Zhou banners to auspicious names—the Azure Dragon, Zouyu, Vermilion Bird, Black Tortoise, Thousand Autumns, and Ten Thousand Years were all his.

literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Left Commander of the Palace Guards.
idiomatic: Soon he was regular attendant, left tutor of the heir, and left palace guard commander.

literal: When Gao Jiong and Su Wei jointly held court power, Ben was very resentful.
idiomatic: When Gao Jiong and Su Wei held power together, Ben was deeply resentful.
